request.spec:
The sheet gains a rounding mode (settings, dated like the floor; SETTING_CHANGED key=rounding
value=<half-up or half-even>; anything else is refused with an error on the settings; blank means
none). A claim whose date has a rounding mode in force rounds every live figure by that mode; a
claim with none in force on its date rounds by the policy date as before.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet gains a rounding mode (settings, dated like the floor; SETTING_CHANGED key=rounding
value=<half-up or half-even>; anything else is refused with an error on the settings; blank means
none). A claim whose date has a rounding mode in force rounds every live figure by that mode; a
claim with none in force on its date rounds by the policy date as before.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The rounding mode is in, and all 4 tests in the spec pass with `bin/e2e`.

**What changed**
- **Saving the setting:** the settings form has a new `setting-rounding` field with its own from-date, and shows the mode in force today in `setting-rounding-current`. A value other than `half-up`, `half-even` or blank shows `settings-error` and saves nothing. The server checks the value too. Values go into the existing per-date settings table, so no migration was needed. Each save writes `SETTING_CHANGED … key=rounding value=<v>`, with ` from=<date>` at the end when a date was typed. The form, its validation and the audit record live in `ValidateSettingsRequest`, `SaveRounding` and `AuditRounding`.
- **How claims round:** a claim uses the rounding mode in force on its date. A correction uses the date of the claim it corrects. With no mode in force, it rounds by the policy date as before. The server applies this everywhere a due is worked out: rollups and totals, due-now, period closing and statements, including statements taken as of a past date. The front end applies the same rule when it works out dues itself (`roundingFor` in `features/rates/rates.ts`).

**One fix outside the request.** Scenario 1 failed every time, on a step that has nothing to do with rounding. When the sheet was viewed as of 2026-03-20, it showed the snapshot line written when the sheet *left* that day. Each step's writes are saved as soon as it runs, so the saved copy of the day already held its own snapshot line. In `today.PUT.yml` the comment says the sheet is kept as it stood first, but the steps were in the opposite order. I moved the step that keeps the day ahead of the snapshot steps, and scenario 1 passed after that.
